_about: The MCP savings study's single definition: what is held fixed, the plan's seed and split, the long task's prompt and its checks. mcp_savings.py reads it; docs/RUNBOOK.md explains it. Its SHA-256 goes into every run record; it is frozen after the pilot.

arms.api: A local Kibana 9.5 is available. Its URL is in the environment variable KIBANA_URL and an API key in KIBANA_TEST_API_KEY. Kibana's API reference is in ./kibana-api/ (kibana.yaml for the whole API, dashboards-api.yaml for the Dashboards and Visualizations APIs).

task.intro: Work in Kibana on its web-logs and flights sample data, held in the indices kibana_sample_data_logs and kibana_sample_data_flights. Do these steps in order:

steps.text: Create a Kibana space with the id '{space}' and the name '{marker} MCP savings'. Do every following step inside that space.
In that space, create a data view on the index kibana_sample_data_logs and one on the index kibana_sample_data_flights, each with its time field set. Name each data view's time field.

Build a dashboard titled '{marker} Web logs' on the web-logs data view with exactly two panels: the number of requests over time, and the number of requests by HTTP response code. Then create an alert rule named '{marker} Server errors' on the web-logs data: it checks every minute and fires when more than 10 server errors arrive within 5 minutes. Count all server errors: every request whose response code is anywhere from 500 to 599. The rule must be enabled when you finish: if it is created disabled, enable it.

Build a dashboard titled '{marker} Flights' on the flights data view with exactly two panels: the number of flights over time, and the number of flights by carrier. Then create an alert rule named '{marker} Cancelled flights' on the flights data: it checks every minute and fires when more than 10 cancelled flights arrive within 5 minutes. The rule must be enabled when you finish: if it is created disabled, enable it.
Change the '{marker} Web logs' dashboard in place, without creating a new dashboard: retitle its response-code panel 'Responses by code', and add a third panel showing the number of requests by host.
Read back what you built: count the panels of the '{marker} Web logs' dashboard, and read the '{marker} Server errors' rule's name, check interval and whether it is enabled.

task.closing:
End your reply with these six lines:
LOGS_TIME_FIELD: <the web-logs data view's time field>
FLIGHTS_TIME_FIELD: <the flights data view's time field>
PANELS: <the number of panels on the '{marker} Web logs' dashboard>
RULE_NAME: <the server-error rule's name>
INTERVAL: <its check interval, such as 5m>
ENABLED: <yes or no>
